headline: Romualdez Served Arrest Warrant in ₱7.44-Billion Plunder Case
seoTitle: Martin Romualdez Arrested in Plunder Case | FMB News
seoDescription: Former House Speaker Martin Romualdez was served an arrest warrant on September 7 after the Sandiganbayan found probable cause in a ₱7.44-billion plunder case. The allegations remain unproven.
deck: Police served former House Speaker Martin Romualdez an arrest warrant and completed booking procedures while he was confined at Cardinal Santos Medical Center. The Sandiganbayan’s probable-cause finding permits the criminal case to proceed; it is not a finding of guilt.
author: FMB News Desk

continuesFrom.headline: Ombudsman Files Plunder Case Against Martin Romualdez Over Alleged Flood-Control Kickback Scheme
continuesFrom.whatChanged: Since FMB News first reported the Ombudsman filing, the Sandiganbayan Third Division found probable cause, issued arrest warrants, and police served Martin Romualdez his warrant and completed booking procedures while he was hospitalized.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Former House Speaker and Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez was served an arrest warrant on September 7 while confined at Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City, according to Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla and multiple news organizations covering the case.

GMA News reported that police read Romualdez the warrant and his rights and completed booking procedures in his hospital room. PNA separately reported that the warrant was served while he remained confined for reported medical concerns.

The Sandiganbayan Third Division issued warrants for Romualdez, former Ako Bicol representative Zaldy Co, Joselyn Tragua Serenio and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra after finding probable cause to proceed on the plunder charge filed by the Office of the Ombudsman. The court stressed that the probable-cause finding does not determine guilt.

sections.heading: What changed since FMB’s first report
paragraphs: FMB News first reported earlier on September 7 that the Ombudsman had filed the plunder case. Since then, the Sandiganbayan Third Division has found probable cause, issued arrest warrants, and authorities have served Romualdez his warrant and completed booking procedures. The earlier report remains intact as the historical first report.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Earlier on September 7, the Office of the Ombudsman filed a plunder case alleging that Romualdez and his co-accused received at least ₱7.44 billion in commissions, kickbacks and other benefits tied to flood-control, infrastructure and other government projects funded from 2022 to 2025.

Romualdez has denied wrongdoing and his legal team has said he will face the allegations through the judicial process. The accusations remain unproven, and all accused are entitled to the presumption of innocence unless guilt is established in court.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The case concerns alleged misuse of public funds intended for infrastructure and flood-control projects, which directly affect public safety, disaster resilience and confidence in government spending.

The arrest is a significant procedural escalation because the controversy has moved from investigation and case filing to active court process. The verified fact is that a court found probable cause for arrest and that the warrant was served; the underlying criminal allegations remain for trial and adjudication.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The next material developments include Romualdez’s presentation before the Sandiganbayan, any court ruling on the conditions of his custody while hospitalized, subsequent pleadings by the defense and prosecution, and further action involving his co-accused.
FMB News will treat future claims about the alleged kickback scheme as allegations unless supported by court findings, official records or independently verified evidence.

The court’s probable-cause finding allows the case to proceed but is not a finding of guilt. FMB News explains what changed and what comes next.
verificationNotes: The central event is verified by GMA News and PNA through statements from Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla and police activity at Cardinal Santos Medical Center.
Reuters and AP independently corroborated the court-ordered arrest and broader case development.
The Sandiganbayan’s probable-cause finding is explicitly distinguished from a finding of guilt.
The ₱7.44-billion figure is presented as the amount alleged by prosecutors, not as proven stolen funds or proven ill-gotten wealth.
